title: Learning by watching and copying
keyIdea: You can learn a new thing by watching someone do it and then copying them. Keep your eyes on the one who shows you, watch all the way to the end, then do the same steps in the same order. If you miss a bit, ask to see it again, slowly.

kid: You can learn by watching. Gran stirs the cake mix. You watch her hands. Then you have a go. That is copying.
Watch it all first. Do not grab the spoon too soon. When Gran is done, it is your turn.
Keep your eyes on the one who shows you. If you look at the dog, you miss it. Do the same steps in the same order: clap, then stomp, then wave.
Missed a bit? That is OK. Say, "Show me again, slowly." Little ones watch you too. They copy what you do.
adult: Toddlers learn a great deal by imitation. From around their first birthday, children copy actions they have seen, and by two and three they can watch a short sequence, such as an action song, stacking cups or wiping a table, and then reproduce it. This topic is about doing that on purpose: watching closely, waiting until the demonstration ends, and copying the steps in order.

The lab gives each part its own action. Children watch Owl's three-move dance and copy it, copy a cup stack by looking at Owl's stack, choose to watch Owl rather than a butterfly, ask to watch the five hand-washing steps again slowly, and then teach Chick a dance and see Chick copy them.

Common mistakes to watch for: starting before the demonstration has finished, copying only one part, swapping the order, and looking away at something more exciting. Another slip is giving up after missing a step rather than asking to see it again. Adults make it harder by showing too fast or by taking over and doing it for the child.

To help, show slowly with few words, name each step as you do it, and pause so your child can have a go. Children copy everything they see, including how we react to mistakes, so show calm second tries.

familyTip: Pick a small job, such as wiping the table or stacking three cups. Say, "Watch my hands," and do it slowly, naming each step. Then say, "Your turn." If a step is missed, show just that part again rather than doing it for them.

visual.caption: What helps you copy? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: watch Owl's dance and copy it, copy a cup stack, keep eyes on Owl, ask to see hand-washing again, then teach Chick.

practice.prompt: Mum shows you how to put on a sock. What do you do first?
practice.hint: To copy, you need to see how it is done.
practice.explain: Watch Mum's hands first. Then you know what to do when it is your turn.

practice.prompt: Owl shows {n} claps, then a stomp. What is the copy?
practice.hint: A copy has the same moves in the same order.
practice.explain: Owl did {n} claps first, then a stomp, so the copy is {n} claps, then a stomp.

practice.prompt: You are copying Dad, but you miss a step. What can you say?
practice.hint: Missing a step is OK. How can you see it again?
practice.explain: Asking to see it again, slowly, lets you catch the step you missed.

practice.prompt: Owl stacks {n} cups. You copy. How many cups go on your stack?
practice.hint: Copying means making it the same as Owl's.
practice.explain: A copy matches Owl, so your stack has {n} cups too, in the same places.

pool.hint: You need to see all of it before you can copy all of it.
pool.explain: Watch to the end first. Then you have seen every step to copy.

pool.prompt: A dog runs past while Gran shows you a song. Where do your eyes go?
pool.hint: Who is showing you the song?
pool.explain: Keep your eyes on Gran. If you watch the dog, you miss the moves.

pool.prompt: Owl waves, then claps. Which is the copy?
pool.hint: Same moves, in the same order as Owl.
pool.explain: Owl waved first and clapped second, so you wave, then clap.

pool.prompt: Tidying up has {n} steps. It is hard to copy. What helps?
pool.hint: Long jobs are easier to see when they go slowly.
pool.explain: Watching the {n} steps again, slowly, helps you see each one.

pool.prompt: Your baby brother watches you stack {n} blocks. What might he do?
pool.hint: Little ones learn by watching big ones.
pool.explain: He saw you stack {n} blocks, so he may try to copy you.

pool.prompt: You copied a dance, but one move was wrong. What now?
choices: Say I am bad at it
pool.hint: A wrong move just means you need to see it once more.
pool.explain: Watch that bit again and try it. Getting a step wrong is part of learning.

pool.prompt: Dad wipes the table. What do you watch?
pool.explain: The job is in Dad's hands and the cloth, so that is where to look.
